div.p:
In his Appendix to his Lectures on the MS. Materials of Ancient Irish History, pp. 472–475, O'Curry has published and translated the story of Baile Binnbérlach from H. 3. 18, p. 47. The same text is found in the British Museum MS Harl. 5280, fo. 48a; with this difference that for many ordinary Irish words (gnáthfhocla) of H.3. 18, Latin, Hebrew, and archaic Irish words have been substituted. We have here, in fact, an instructive example of that delight in obscure modes of diction, which Irish poetry so often shows in its use of kennings, extinct forms of language, antiquated native, and
lastly even foreign words. We know that a regular training in the use of such expressions formed part of the curriculum of the aspiring fili, and I think that it was these various modes of expression that were comprehended under the name of bérla na filed "the language or dialect of the poets", which the young fili, then called anroth, was required to master in the sixth year of his apprenticeship. See Thurneysen, Irische Texte, vol. III, I, p. 38. An amusing example of the use of such language occurs in Cormac's Glossary, s.v. lethech.

While in a literary point of view the use of the incongruous elements, misplaced fragments of learning, only serves to mar a pretty tale, it supplies the modern student with some valuable linguistic material. For this reason I have thought it worth while to publish the following text. I add a translation and a glossary of the old and rare words.

div0.head: Scél Baili Binnbérlaig
div0.p:
Baili Binnberlach mac Buain. Tri hui Cabha maic Cinga maic Rosa maic Rudraigi: Monach &ersir; Baili &ersir; Fercorb, de quibus Dal m-Buain &ersir; Dal Cuirb &ersir; Monaig Arad. Oenmac Buain .i. Baili. Ba saincais-seom di Aillinn filia
Lugdach bein Fergusai Goo, no di deir Eogain maic Dathi &ersir; ba sainamor do cech oen atchid &ersir; dicechlad eter issai &ersir; genai ar a urriseib. Corrusdailset coir dala i n-dormainecht ic Ros na Turigin occ Laind Moelduib ar bru Boinne Breg.

Dogene an uir atuaid dia torrachtoin o Eomuin Machi tar Sliauh Fuaid &ersir; tar Teme Muiri co Traig m-Baili. Ro turnaid a n-drubai &ersir; russcuirid a n-gabrai for an rindiuc dia gleth. Digensad ainius &ersir; oibnius.

A m-botar ann conacatar elpoid uathmor ænnoé cugo
indes. Ba hudmall a rem &ersir; a ascnamh. Meti les noraited in trogain sín sighi seig di aild no clo do glasréin. A clipio fri tir. Ar a cind! ol Baile, conatcomaircter nde cid ted no canus tanuic no cia fath a cudnoidh. Di Tuaig-Inbir tiagoim &ersir; tar ais budthuaid anussai o
Slioab Suidiu Laigeon &ersir; nintha do imtecht liumm acht no Lugdach maic Fergusai tuc grad do Baili mac Buain &ersir; tainic dia dal, corucsat oic Laigevn fuirri &ersir; bathaid, amail rusgellsad draide &ersir; degfaidi doib, na comraicdis a m-bethaid et conricfaidis iarna nás &ersir; nach scerdais tre bithu sir. Is
siad sin mo scelai. &ersir; 'musteti uaib iermo &ersir; niptar cuimgech a fostad. Otcechlai Baile anni sin crinniur marb cin anima &ersir; clandtair a fert &ersir; a raith &ersir; saitir a airne &ersir; dogniter a oenuch guba la hUllto. &ersir; lossaig eo trian lige combo reil delb &ersir; fuaith capaid Baili for a
ind, unde dixid Traigh m-Baili.

Iarom 'musla buddes in fer cetno co forad a m-bai an ingen Aildinn &ersir; docing isan grianan. Can tic anti nat aithgenamar? ol ind ingen. A fochlai Erend o Tuaig-Inbir &ersir; secha so co Sliab Suidi Laigen. Scelai lat? ol
in ingen. Ni fuil sceloi is cointi sund, acht adconnorc Ultai ac oenuch guba et oc cloidi ratha &ersir; ic sadad lia &ersir; ac graifned a anma Baili maic Buain rigdamnoi Ulad do thin Trago Baili, et se ic torrachtain lennain &ersir; mna serce dia tard tal, ar ni fuil a scoth doib coristais a m-bethaid no
nech dib d'faircsin aroili ina m-biu. Dobidg amach iar n-indiuld an misceoil. Difuit Aillinn marb cin anmoin &ersir; claitir a fert &ersir;rl. Et assoid abhold trian lige &ersir; ba gesco mor a cind septimo anno, &ersir; fethol chuid Aillinne for a uachtar.

A cind secht m-bliadan dana tescait mail &ersir; faidi &ersir; fisidi int év boi os Baili &ersir; 'musgniet tauhull filiud nde &ersir; scribait fise &ersir; fese &ersir; serco &ersir; tochmarco Ulad inni. Fon fiu cetni scriutar tochmarco Laigen inti-si.

Doruacht ant samhuin iarsuidi &ersir; dogniter a fes la hArt
mac Quind. Tolotatar dil &ersir; aes cacha danai fon fes sin amail ba bes &ersir; doradsad a taibli leo. &ersir; dusci Art &ersir; otconnairc 'muscomairc. Et tucad cuce in di tabald co m-batar ina lamoib eneuch a n-inchoib. Imusling an tabold for araili dib cor' imnaisced amail fethlind im urslait. Et ni
tualaing a n-imscarad &ersir; batar amail gach sed isan taisced i Temraig, curusloisc Dunlang mac Enda diar'ort an in-genraid, unde dixit:
Aboll Aildinde ardai,
ibor Baili, becc forboi,
cia dobertar au laidhe,
ni tuicid daine borba.

Et amail adbert ingen Cormaic ui Quinn:
Es fris samlaim Aluime,
fri hibor Traga Baili,
fris combaroim aroili,
frisan abaild a hAili.

Fland mac Lonain dixit:
Desid Cormac im cel coir
conid fris format ant ⋅luaig,
tabrad Dia airi noeb nár
in craeb do Traig Baili buain.
Forbuir bili buidnip reb,
rolaa a delb truimib tor,
diarcelgad rocelgaid fir
amlaid sin rocelgaid cor.
